{"data": {"id": "3802", "type": "newsItem", "attributes": {"headline": "Harrow & Finch Bank lowers its business reference rate", "slug": "harrow-finch-bank-lowers-its-business-reference-rate", "publishedAt": "2026-08-18T11:45:00+01:00", "byline": "Mara Ellery", "content": [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Harrow & Finch Bank will reduce its business reference rate from 6.50% to 6.25% on 24 August. The change applies to lending agreements that track the bank’s reference rate. Fixed-rate loans will keep their agreed rates until the end of their fixed terms."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "A company with a KRN 2 million loan priced at the reference rate plus 2 percentage points would pay around KRN 417 less interest over a full month, assuming its balance stays unchanged. Actual savings will depend on the number of days in the interest period and the outstanding balance."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The bank is sending notices to affected borrowers this week. Customers do not need to submit a request to receive the reduction. Relationship teams in Saltmarsh, Kestrel Bay, Ostara, Amberford and Val-Brume can explain how the change will appear on individual statements."}]}}}

{"data": {"id": "3809", "type": "newsItem", "attributes": {"headline": "New equipment lending programme opens with forty million crowns", "slug": "new-equipment-lending-programme-opens-with-forty-million", "publishedAt": "2026-08-24T14:15:00+01:00", "byline": "Devran Holt", "content": [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Harrow & Finch Bank today opened a KRN 40 million lending programme for mid-sized companies replacing production equipment. Businesses across Kestria can apply for loans of between KRN 250,000 and KRN 4 million, with repayment terms of three to seven years."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Eligible purchases include workshop machinery, commercial refrigeration and equipment used to sort or pack goods. Applicants must provide equipment quotations, their latest accounts and a cash-flow forecast. The bank will assess whether repayments remain affordable during quieter trading periods. Purchased equipment will normally form part of the security."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Both existing customers and companies new to the bank may apply. Interest rates and arrangement fees will be set for each borrower and disclosed before an agreement is signed. Applications are open through the bank’s lending teams, including its industrial business desks in Amberford and Kestrel Bay."}]}}}

{"data": {"id": "3816", "type": "newsItem", "attributes": {"headline": "Bank publishes revised fees for business lending administration", "slug": "bank-publishes-revised-fees-for-business-lending-administration", "publishedAt": "2026-09-02T09:00:00+01:00", "byline": "Leonie Venn", "content": [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Harrow & Finch Bank has published a revised schedule of business lending administration fees, taking effect on 5 October. The fee for a borrower-requested security amendment will fall from KRN 450 to KRN 325. Providing a duplicate annual interest certificate will become free, replacing the current KRN 35 charge."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The fee for reviewing a request to extend an overdraft temporarily will rise from KRN 175 to KRN 225. It covers the review and does not guarantee approval. Customers will be told whether a charge applies before they ask the bank to proceed with any chargeable work."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The changes do not alter agreed loan margins or repayment dates. Where an existing agreement fixes an administration fee, that agreement will continue to apply. The full schedule is available from relationship teams and on the bank’s website, with copies in French available for customers in Val-Brume."}]}}}

{"data": {"id": "3823", "type": "newsItem", "attributes": {"headline": "Val-Brume lending desk adds appointments for French-speaking businesses", "slug": "val-brume-lending-desk-adds-appointments-for-french", "publishedAt": "2026-09-03T15:30:00+01:00", "byline": "Tomas Arlen", "content": [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Harrow & Finch Bank has added twelve weekly appointments at its Val-Brume lending desk for businesses that prefer to discuss borrowing in French. The additional sessions are available on Tuesdays and Thursdays and can be held at the branch or by telephone."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Appointments cover working capital, equipment purchases and reviews of existing facilities. Businesses can request a document checklist in French before their meeting. The desk will also help customers identify which financial records are needed, although it cannot prepare accounts or provide independent legal advice."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "There is no appointment charge and no obligation to apply for a loan. Lending decisions remain subject to the bank’s usual affordability and security checks. The expansion follows a six-week booking review in which the Val-Brume team recorded an average wait of nine working days for a French-language lending appointment."}]}}}

{"data": {"id": "3830", "type": "newsItem", "attributes": {"headline": "Business reference rate falls by a further quarter point", "slug": "business-reference-rate-falls-by-a-further-quarter", "publishedAt": "2026-09-18T14:45:00+01:00", "byline": "Mara Ellery", "content": [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Harrow & Finch Bank will lower its business reference rate from 6.25% to 6.00% on 21 September. Borrowers whose agreements track this rate will receive the reduction automatically. The change follows the quarter-point reduction that took effect on 24 August."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Together, the two changes reduce annual interest by KRN 5,000 on an unchanged KRN 1 million balance, before any fees and subject to the terms of the agreement. Fixed-rate borrowing is unaffected. Loans linked to a different reference rate will continue to follow the calculation set out in their contracts."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The bank reviewed its funding costs and lending commitments before making the decision. Updated repayment information will be sent where monthly payments change. Customers with interest-only facilities will see the new rate applied to the relevant days in their next interest calculation and can request a breakdown from their relationship team."}]}}}

{"data": {"id": "3837", "type": "newsItem", "attributes": {"headline": "Equipment programme expands after strong demand from regional manufacturers", "slug": "equipment-programme-expands-after-strong-demand-from-regional", "publishedAt": "2026-09-28T14:30:00+01:00", "byline": "Devran Holt", "content": [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Harrow & Finch Bank has increased its equipment lending programme from KRN 40 million to KRN 60 million. Since applications opened on 24 August, the bank has approved KRN 26.4 million across 19 facilities. Of that amount, KRN 11.8 million has been drawn by borrowers."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Companies in Amberford and Ostara account for just over half the approved lending by value. Purchases include cutting machines, temperature-controlled storage and packing lines. Approval totals represent agreed facilities rather than equipment already installed, and borrowers draw funds as supplier invoices become due."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The additional allocation is available to new applications from today. Loan sizes remain between KRN 250,000 and KRN 4 million, with terms of three to seven years. Each application will receive a separate credit assessment. Businesses should obtain approval before relying on bank funding to place a binding equipment order."}]}}}

{"data": {"id": "3844", "type": "newsItem", "attributes": {"headline": "Revised administration fees take effect for business borrowers today", "slug": "revised-administration-fees-take-effect-for-business-borrowers", "publishedAt": "2026-10-05T15:30:00+01:00", "byline": "Leonie Venn", "content": [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "The business lending administration fees announced by Harrow & Finch Bank on 2 September take effect today. A borrower-requested security amendment now costs KRN 325, down from KRN 450. Duplicate annual interest certificates are now free, removing the previous KRN 35 charge."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Reviewing a request for a temporary overdraft extension now costs KRN 225, an increase of KRN 50. The review fee does not depend on whether the request is approved. Staff must explain the applicable fee and obtain the customer’s agreement before starting a chargeable review."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Requests accepted before today will be charged under the previous schedule. Existing contracts that specify a fixed administration fee retain that fee. Customers can obtain the current schedule from any lending team or download it from the bank’s website. A French-language version is also available through the Val-Brume desk."}]}}}

{"data": {"id": "3851", "type": "newsItem", "attributes": {"headline": "Ostara businesses offered working capital review appointments this month", "slug": "ostara-businesses-offered-working-capital-review-appointments-this", "publishedAt": "2026-10-06T09:00:00+01:00", "byline": "Tomas Arlen", "content": [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Harrow & Finch Bank is offering 30 working capital review appointments for mid-sized businesses at its Ostara branch between 12 and 30 October. The sessions are intended for companies preparing for seasonal changes in stock purchases, customer payments or supplier bills."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Each appointment lasts up to an hour and carries no charge. Businesses should bring a thirteen-week cash-flow forecast, a list of unpaid customer invoices and details of existing borrowing. A relationship manager will discuss the timing of expected receipts and payments and identify any information needed for a lending application."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Attendance does not require a company to move its banking arrangements. Any subsequent request for an overdraft or loan will be assessed separately, with rates and fees explained before acceptance. Telephone appointments are available for businesses outside Ostara that cannot attend the branch during the scheduled period."}]}}}

{"data": {"id": "3858", "type": "newsItem", "attributes": {"headline": "Bank introduces clearer monthly statements for variable-rate business loans", "slug": "bank-introduces-clearer-monthly-statements-for-variable-rate", "publishedAt": "2026-10-13T14:45:00+01:00", "byline": "Leonie Venn", "content": [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Harrow & Finch Bank has introduced a revised monthly statement layout for variable-rate business loans. Statements issued from today show the reference rate, the borrower’s agreed margin and the number of days charged at each rate in a single interest table."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Where a rate changes during the statement period, separate rows show the balance and calculation for each part of that period. This will help borrowers check interest following the bank’s reference rate reductions in August and September. Fees will continue to appear separately from interest."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The layout changes how information is presented and does not alter loan terms or payment dates. It was tested with 24 business customers from Saltmarsh, Amberford and Val-Brume. Large-print statements and an explanation in French are available on request. Customers who need help checking a calculation can contact the lending team named on their statement."}]}}}

{"data": {"id": "3865", "type": "newsItem", "attributes": {"headline": "Kestrel Bay lending team moves to larger customer premises", "slug": "kestrel-bay-lending-team-moves-to-larger-customer", "publishedAt": "2026-10-16T16:00:00+01:00", "byline": "Tomas Arlen", "content": [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Harrow & Finch Bank’s Kestrel Bay lending team will move to 18 Lantern Quay on 19 October. The new premises provide four private meeting rooms, compared with two at the current office, and a ground-floor entrance with step-free access from the pavement."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The office will serve mid-sized companies seeking lending advice and support with existing facilities. Customer telephone numbers and relationship managers will remain the same. Meetings already booked for 19 October onwards will take place at Lantern Quay, and the bank is contacting customers individually with directions."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The current office at 7 Tern Passage closes to visitors at 16:00 today. Telephone support will remain available during normal opening hours throughout the move. The new office opens at 09:00 on 19 October. It is an appointment-based lending office and does not provide cash deposits, withdrawals or counter payment services."}]}}}

{"data": {"id": "3872", "type": "newsItem", "attributes": {"headline": "Half-year results show lending growth and higher impairment charges", "slug": "half-year-results-show-lending-growth-and-higher", "publishedAt": "2026-10-21T10:45:00+01:00", "byline": "Mara Ellery", "content": [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Harrow & Finch Bank today reported profit before tax of KRN 18.6 million for the six months ended 30 September 2026, compared with KRN 17.9 million a year earlier. Operating income rose to KRN 52.4 million from KRN 48.7 million, while operating costs increased to KRN 27.1 million from KRN 25.6 million."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The charge for expected lending losses increased to KRN 6.7 million from KRN 5.2 million. The increase mainly reflected weaker repayment prospects among a small number of wholesale borrowers. Gross customer lending reached KRN 1.24 billion at the period end, up from KRN 1.17 billion on 31 March 2026."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "New lending drawn during the half year totalled KRN 186 million. Customer deposits stood at KRN 1.41 billion on 30 September. The bank continued to fund equipment purchases and working capital across Kestria while reviewing borrowers showing early signs of payment difficulty. The results are unaudited."}]}}}

{"data": {"id": "3879", "type": "newsItem", "attributes": {"headline": "New borrower support team offers earlier repayment difficulty reviews", "slug": "new-borrower-support-team-offers-earlier-repayment-difficulty", "publishedAt": "2026-10-22T08:00:00+01:00", "byline": "Devran Holt", "content": [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Harrow & Finch Bank has established a dedicated borrower support team for business customers facing repayment difficulties. The five-person team is based in Saltmarsh and accepts referrals from relationship managers across Kestria. Customers can also ask their usual lending contact for a support review."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The team will examine recent trading, cash forecasts and existing repayment commitments. Depending on the circumstances, options may include changing payment dates or agreeing a temporary reduction in principal repayments. Any arrangement requires an assessment and written agreement. Interest may continue to accrue, and extending a loan can increase its total cost."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "There is no charge for the initial support review. Customers are encouraged to make contact as soon as they expect a shortfall, even if every payment is currently up to date. French-language reviews are available through the Val-Brume lending desk. Requesting a review does not itself change contractual payment obligations."}]}}}
